analysis_notes.source_text_analysis: The full text of Torah #269 is: 'מִדִּירַת הַצַּדִּיק נִכָּר מַעֲשֵׂה הַדּוֹר. וְסִימָן לַדָּבָר: וְהִיא יוֹשֶׁבֶת תַּחַת תֹּמֶר (שופטים ד:ה), וְאָמְרוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מגילה יד): מַה תָּמָר אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא לֵב אֶחָד אַף יִשְׂרָאֵל כֵּן'. This is a pure aphorism — a concise teaching without extended analysis. The Rebbe does NOT use the word 'בְּחִינַת' anywhere in the text. The analogy structure used is the Talmudic 'מַה...אַף' (just as...so too), which expresses similarity rather than identity of essence. This does not constitute a bechina relationship in the technical sense used by the dataset. The four concepts listed above appear in the text but are not assigned to any package because no packages exist for this Torah.
